reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

posts.text: Reminder that the annual Medicare Open Enrollment Period is underway for Medicare beneficiaries across California's Third Congressional District. From October 15 through December 7, 2026, eligible individuals can review their current Medicare coverage, compare available health and prescription drug plans, and make changes for 2027. https://t.co/VlXvlf1FYW

This week, I sent a letter to the California Department of Education urging them to investigate the recent hack of Educational Testing Services that exposed the personal information of millions of California students, including their names, addresses, date of birth, disability statuses, assessment results, and testing accommodations.

I am calling on the Department to prioritize and expedite this investigation that revealed private information of millions of students and their families. These families deserve answers, and what is being done to ensure this never happens again.

Kaiser Permanente breaks ground on a new healthcare center in Folsom!

Yesterday, I joined the groundbreaking ceremony for a new 187,000-square-foot outpatient facility that will include 60 clinical offices offering a wide range of care options in one convenient location.

Some of these services include urgent care, mental health services, expanded outpatient surgery, advanced imaging, and much more.

Read more about the project here: https://t.co/nNPJAlzvRC

Our work on your behalf continues, and I encourage you to contact us as you normally would for assistance with casework, constituent service requests, meeting requests, or any other questions or concerns. It was an honor to recognize Chief Reginald Williams of the Rocklin Fire Department on his retirement after 32 years in the fire service, including six years serving the City of Rocklin. 

Chief Williams has earned the respect and admiration of the firefighters he has led and the residents he has served. His tireless work has strengthened the Rocklin Fire Department and helped position it to meet the needs of the community for years to come. Thank you, Chief Williams, for your outstanding service and commitment to public safety. I wish you a happy and fulfilling retirement.

Congratulations to Chief Billiter on assuming the role. I look forward to working with you!

I am pleased to announce that my office is once again hosting the 2026 Congressional App Challenge. This competition is aimed at encouraging middle and high school students to learn how to code by creating their own applications. The challenge highlights the value of computer science and STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Math) education.

Each app will be graded by an independent panel, and all awards will be commemorated with a Congressional Certificate of Recognition and will be displayed on my website. Last year, more than 4,600 original apps were submitted from students across the country that focused on real-world challenges ranging from health and accessibility to education, sustainability, and civic engagement.

Additionally, the first-place winner(s) will receive an invitation to the #Houseofcode Celebration located in Washington, D.C., and the winning app will be:
• Displayed in the U.S. Capitol Building 
• Featured on the House of Representatives’ website (https://t.co/O13iznmu3h)

The deadline to submit an app is October 26 at 9:00am PT, and you can submit here: https://t.co/iDqLqBovNa See less

It was great to be with the San Juan Water District and members of the community yesterday to celebrate the progress being made on the Kokila Reservoir Replacement Project.

This is an important investment in our community’s water infrastructure, and I’m proud to have helped secure over a million dollars in federal funding to support this project.

The Kokila Reservoir has served our community for more than 40 years, providing water storage for San Juan Water District and being an essential backup during emergencies.

This project will not only modernize aging infrastructure, but will also help ensure the continued delivery of safe and reliable drinking water to the many customers it serves.

Yesterday, I attended the Semper Fi Association of Lincoln and the Southwest Placer County Toys for Tots kickoff of the 79th annual toy collection season. 

Last year, 27,903 toys were collected and given to 12,480 children across Southwest Placer County and local cities through 17 charities and a family distribution event. 

This tremendous outpouring of supporting, to assure every child can experience the joy of the holiday season, says so much about the values of our area. Find out where you can drop off a toy here. https://t.co/OVcor6sh74

If there is any issue that shouldn't be partisan, it is stopping fraud. And California unfortunately has more of it than any state. $32 billion in unemployment fraud alone.

When fraudsters steal unemployment funds, people out of work lose support.

When fraudsters steal SNAP benefits, hungry families lose meals.

When fraudsters steal Medi-Cal funds, patients lose care.

When fraudsters steal homelessness funds, people lose shelter.

When fraudsters steal financial aid, students lose educational opportunities.

When fraudsters steal hospice funds, people lose comfort and dignity at the end of life.

When fraudsters steal veterans’ benefits, those who served so valiantly lose support.

When fraudsters steal SBA funds, local businesses lose help.

When fraudsters steal workers’ comp funds, injured workers lose treatment.

When fraudsters steal child care funds, working families lose care for their kids.

We've sent a bipartisan, bicameral letter to the Interior Secretary opposing any plan to turn over part of Yosemite to private development. Yosemite is a national treasure that must always belong to the public. https://t.co/EOpxzkvd49

Today we remember all who lost their lives on one of the most tragic and fateful days in our nation’s history 25 years ago. 

It is also an occasion to remember how we saw America at its very best: from the heroism of our first responders and ordinary citizens, to the way we came together as a country and put all of our differences aside.

Perhaps the best tribute we can pay is to find ways of recapturing that spirit of American unity.

Californians never voted to ban gas cars. Californians never voted to ban tires. Californians never voted for a new healthcare tax – to the contrary, they expressly forbade it.  

We're fighting to protect the will of California voters from the schemes of Sacramento politicians. https://t.co/yz9ysmhZPW

Yosemite is a national treasure that belongs to the public. I am absolutely opposed to turning over any part of it for private development and am asking the Secretary of the Interior to abandon any such plans. https://t.co/omouZ4hDMP

I'm calling on Governor Newsom to reverse the recently imposed Tire Ban. This will take 70 percent of tires off the market and cost consumers hundreds of dollars.

Californians simply can't afford it. https://t.co/4uTJYoZWgb

This week we celebrated National Intern Day. It was a pleasure to have Gianna (Senior at University of Connecticut), Madeline (Senior at Harvard), and Caitlyn (Sophomore at UC Berkeley) serve in my DC office this summer. Thank you for all your hard work this summer on behalf of my constituents in #CA03!

We are formally asking the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to block Newsom's new healthcare tax. Voters expressly prohibited him from imposing such a tax, which will increase premiums by up to $400 for California families. https://t.co/LJxBmAbcgr
https://t.co/gvEL8FPUTq

A new poll shows two-thirds of Californians oppose Newsom's ban on gas cars, which he imposed without a vote of any kind.  

Fortunately, my Resolution overturning the ban passed with bipartisan support and is now law. The will of the people prevailed. https://t.co/aW8ikYEFCO
A tremendous honor and a tribute to the incredible work of our district office team. We always put constituent service first. https://t.co/dTvYRz4eb6

Governor Gavin Newsom just signed a new healthcare tax that will increase premiums for Californians by hundreds of dollars. This defies the will of our voters, who passed Prop. 35 to limit such tax increases.   

This is simply something that our state cannot afford. In a formal letter, I am asking HHS to block the implementation of this tax proposal.

I would like to invite you to a Government Job Fair hosted by my office on Monday, August 3 from 10am - 3pm at the Rocklin Event Center. 

Join us to learn about career opportunities with dozens of federal, state, and local government agencies. This event is a great chance to connect directly with government job recruiters, submit your resume, learn about a wide range of careers, and explore rewarding jobs in public service.

RSVP here: https://t.co/DoODq3GaF9

Today, I spoke on the House Floor in support of H.R. 3104, the Ukrainian Adjustment Act. 

This legislation would adjust their status to lawful permit resident. It’s the right thing to do for these individuals and their families. It’s the right thing to do for our economy and for communities across this country.

Last week, USA Properties broke ground on The Steven, a 180-home affordable senior apartment community in Rocklin. 
This new complex will provide affordable apartment homes for our seniors, helping address the growing need for affordable housing in Placer County. 
Legislation I supported in 2025, H.R. 1, helps make projects like this possible. https://t.co/IWooTeWgZC

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
